$comment: Language-neutral behaviour every StackLens SDK must show. Each SDK ships a runner that implements these scenarios with its own instrumentation and prints {"<scenario>": TraceRecord, ...} as JSON; check.mjs validates the output. Span names are ClassName.method (or the closest idiom in the language, mapped to these names).

scenarios.name: nested-calls
scenarios.description: A job calls OrderController.create(input) → OrderService.place(input) → OrderRepository.save(order), which returns { id: 1, ...order }.

scenarios.name: error
scenarios.description: A job calls PaymentService.charge(amount) which throws an error named PaymentError with message "card declined". The job does not catch it.

scenarios.name: repeated-calls
scenarios.description: A job calls BatchService.run() which calls BatchHelper.step(i) 1000 times in a loop (synchronously).

scenarios.name: logs
scenarios.description: A job calls AuditService.record(event), which attaches the log line "recorded" to the current call (stacklens.log or the language's logging hook).

scenarios.name: cross-service
scenarios.description: Two instrumented HTTP services. A job (the caller) sends GET /orders/1 with the language's standard HTTP client to a second, instrumented HTTP server (the callee), which responds 200 with JSON { "id": 1 }. The runner outputs the caller's trace under "cross-service" and the callee's trace under "cross-service.child". The outgoing call is one span of kind http with `outbound` set; the request carries a W3C traceparent header naming that span; the callee's trace records it as `parent` and returns its own trace id in the x-stacklens-trace-id response header.
